(Capacity: 13,819) | champion = | tourney = [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] | tourney_result = Sweet Sixteen }} {{2021–22 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2021–22 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] during the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22 NCAA Division I season]]. The [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|Bruins]] were led by third-year head coach [[Mick Cronin (basketball)|Mick Cronin]] and they played their home games at [[Pauley Pavilion]] as members of the [[Pac-12 Conference]]. All ten players from the previous year's [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#Final Four|Final Four]] team returned. [[Johnny Juzang]] earned third-team [[2022 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors,{{cite news|first=Bruce|last=Pascoe|title=NABC names Arizona's Bennedict Mathurin second-team all-American|date=March 16, 2022|website=Tucson.com|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/nabc-names-arizonas-bennedict-mathurin-second-team-all-american/article_feeddc06-a556-11ec-b484-ffd76def638a.html|access-date=March 17, 2022}} and he was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] along with [[Tyger Campbell]] and [[Jaime Jaquez Jr.]] Jaquez, [[Jaylen Clark]] and [[Myles Johnson]] were also voted to the Pac-12 All-Defensive team.{{cite news|first=Ryan|last=Kartje|title=UCLA’s Johnny Juzang, USC’s Isaiah Mobley among All-Pac-12 picks for Bruins, Trojans|date=March 8, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/story/2022-03-08/all-pac-12-ucla-usc|access-date=March 8, 2022}} New this season is that the team's footwear, apparel, and equipment are provided by [[Air Jordan|Jordan Brand]] and [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]]. UCLA was ranked nationally in the top 10 for most of the season.{{cite web|first=Dylan|last=Hernandez|title=Column: UCLA’s woeful offense needs a Mick Cronin overhaul to be Final Four worthy|date=January 26, 2023|work=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/story/2023-01-26/ucla-offense-usc-loss-ncaa-tournament|access-date=January 27, 2023}} They began the season 5–0 before facing [[2021–22 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]] in a rematch of the Final Four from the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2021 NCAA tournament]].{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title= No. 2 UCLA defeats Bellarmine in tuneup before Final Four rematch with Gonzaga|date=November 22, 2021|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2021-11-22/ucla-mens-basketball-defeats-bellarmine-gonzaga|access-date=December 21, 2021}} However, the No. 2 Bruins suffered their first defeat in an 83–63 blowout to the No. 1 Bulldogs.{{cite news|first=Adam|last=Zagoria|title=When No. 1 Is a Lot Better Than No. 2|date=November 24, 2021|newspaper=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/11/24/sports/ncaabasketball/gonzaga-ucla.html|access-date=December 21, 2021}} The UCLA team experienced a [[COVID-19]] outbreak starting on December 15, 2021, causing them to cancel three nonconference games and postpone two Pac-12 games.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=After lengthy pause, UCLA basketball will resume playing Wednesday against Arizona State|date=January 2, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-01-02/after-lengthy-pause-ucla-basketball-will-resume-playing-wednesday-against-arizona-state|access-date=January 4, 2022}} The Bruins resumed play on January 6, 2022, against [[2021–22 Long Beach State Beach men's basketball team|Long Beach State]]. At this time, the team began to play [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] due to COVID-19 restrictions on indoor events implemented by the campus.{{Cite web|date=2022-01-05|title=Fans won't be able to pump up the volume at UCLA basketball's long-awaited return|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-01-05/fans-wont-be-able-to-pump-up-the-volume-in-ucla-basketballs-long-awaited-return|access-date=2022-01-14|website=Los Angeles Times|language=en-US}} The rematch against the Beach, who UCLA defeated earlier in November, was scheduled after the Bruins' original opponents that week, [[2021–22 Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball team|Arizona State]] and [[2021–22 Stanford Cardinal men's basketball team|Stanford]], needed to postpone due to coronavirus issues in their programs. It was the first time UCLA faced a nonconference opponent twice in the same regular season since [[1982–83 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|1982–83]], when they faced [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] in a home and away series.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Fans won’t be able to pump up the volume at UCLA basketball’s long-awaited return|date=January 5, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-01-05/fans-wont-be-able-to-pump-up-the-volume-in-ucla-basketballs-long-awaited-return|access-date=January 9, 2022}} The Bruins lost in overtime to [[2021–22 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]] on January 13, their first defeat since late November.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=No. 3 UCLA struggles on defense in 'embarrassing' overtime loss to Oregon|date=January 13, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-01-13/ucla-mens-basketball-loses-oregon|access-date=February 13, 2022}} UCLA then won six straight conference games, including their sixth consecutive over [[Arizona–UCLA men's basketball rivalry|rival]] [[2021–22 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]],{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=No. 7 UCLA conjures March Madness intensity in dominating win over No. 3 Arizona|date=January 25, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-01-25/ucla-mens-basketball-defeats-arizona-pac-12|access-date=February 14, 2022}} to gain sole possession of first place in the Pac-12.{{cite news|title=No. 7 UCLA beats Stanford 66-43 for 6th straight win|date=January 30, 2022|website=ESPN.com|agency=AP|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401377438|access-date=February 13, 2022}} However, the Bruins lost their third game in four contests after falling to their crosstown rivals, [[2021–22 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]]. It was their fifth straight loss to the Trojans, their longest drought in [[UCLA–USC rivalry|the series]] since the 1940s.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=Five fixes that could help UCLA pull out of the nosedive that threatens its season|date=February 13, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/story/2022-02-13/fix-fixes-that-could-help-ucla-pull-out-of-the-nosedive-that-threatens-its-season|access-date=February 14, 2022}} UCLA ended the regular season winning six of their last seven games.{{cite news|first=Bill|last=Plaschke|title=March Madness is nearly here, and UCLA is ready to go dancing|date=March 6, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/story/2022-03-06/ucla-mens-basketball-ncaa-tournament-march-madness|access-date=March 6, 2022}} They won their regular-season finale against USC to claim the No. 2 seed in the [[2022 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|Pac-12 tournament]], breaking their tie with the Trojans for second place in the conference. It was the Bruins' first win in the series since February 2019, and their first under Cronin.{{cite news|title=No. 17 UCLA beats No. 16 USC 75-68, finishes 2nd in Pac-12|date=March 5, 2022|website=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401377493|access-date=March 6, 2022}} UCLA advanced to the Pac-12 Tournament championship game, where they lost to Arizona.{{cite news|title=Arizona’s size proves too much for UCLA in Pac-12 title game|date=March 12, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2022/03/12/arizonas-size-proves-too-much-for-ucla-in-pac-12-title-game/|access-date=March 18, 2022}} It was the Bruins' first appearance in the title game since their win in [[2014 Pac-12 Conference men's basketball tournament|2014]] over the Wildcats.{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA defeats rival USC, advances to Pac-12 basketball tournament title game|date=March 11, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/story/2022-03-11/ucla-defeats-usc-advances-to-pac-12-basketball-tournament-final|access-date=March 18, 2022}}{{cite news|first=Justin|last=Spears|title=Arizona Wildcats to meet UCLA in Pac-12 Tournament championship, season rubber match|date=March 11, 2022|website=Tucson.com|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/arizona-wildcats-to-meet-ucla-in-pac-12-tournament-championship-season-rubber-match/article_a8023afe-a1cd-11ec-ab4c-d312fa043005.html|access-date=March 18, 2022}} Seeded No. 4 in the East Regional of the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], UCLA rallied in the opener for a 57–53 comeback win over 13th-seeded [[2021–22 Akron Zips men's basketball team|Akron]]. Campbell scored eight of the Bruins' final 10 points,{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA rallies to beat Akron and advance in the NCAA tournament|date=March 17, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-03-17/ucla-rallies-to-beat-akron-and-advance-in-the-ncaa-tournament|access-date=March 18, 2022}} and he finished with a team-high 16.{{cite news|first=Tarek|last=Fattal|title=Tyger Campbell, UCLA fend off Akron in NCAA Tournament opener|date=March 18, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2022/03/17/tyger-campbell-ucla-fend-off-akron-in-ncaa-tournament-opener/|access-date=March 19, 2022}} The Bruins defeated fifth-seeded [[2021–22 Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball team|Saint Mary's]] 72–56 to advance to the Sweet 16 in consecutive seasons for the first time since [[2014–15 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2015]].{{cite news|first=Ben|last=Bolch|title=UCLA defeats St. Mary’s to return to the Sweet 16 for the second straight year|date=March 19, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/ucla/story/2022-03-19/ucla-defeats-saint-marys-ncaa-tournament-march-madness-sweet-16|access-date=March 19, 2022}} UCLA was eliminated in the semifinals in a 73–66 loss to eighth-seeded [[2021–22 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]]. The Bruins led by three points with two minutes remaining in a game that featured 14 lead changes and eight ties.{{cite news|first=Eddie|last=Pells|title=If the shoe fits: Love leads Carolina over UCLA into Elite 8|date=March 25, 2022|publisher=Associated Press|url=https://apnews.com/article/march-madness-north-carolina-tar-heels-mens-basketball-st-peters-peacocks-mens-basketball-ucla-bruins-mens-basketball-sports-2a42c4860b70e73463551d9840189bc2|access-date=March 26, 2022}}{{cite news|first=Jim|last=Alexander|title=Alexander: Others have NCAA magic this year, but UCLA’s runs out|date=March 26, 2022|newspaper=Los Angeles Daily News|url=https://www.dailynews.com/2022/03/25/alexander-others-have-ncaa-magic-this-year-but-uclas-runs-out/|access-date=March 26, 2022|quote=And for much of the night, the Bruins (27-8) were up to the task in a game with a blistering pace, 14 lead changes and eight ties.}} On March 25, assistant coach [[Michael Lewis (basketball coach)|Michael Lewis]] was named as head coach of [[Ball State Cardinals men's basketball|Ball State]] basketball team. ==Previous season== {{main|2020–21 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team}} The Bruins are coming off of a season in which they made an improbable run in the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] to the [[Final Four]], where their upset bid against top-ranked [[2020–21 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]] in the National Semifinal fell just short in overtime, 93–90. UCLA, which had begun the tournament in the First Four, became just the fifth 11-seed to ever advance to the Final Four.
